title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 1
paragraphs: Mardonius, when Alexander had returned and reported to him what the Athenians had said, set out from Thessaly and began leading his army with all diligence toward Athens, taking up with him the people of whatever land he passed through. The leaders of Thessaly, meanwhile, were not sorry for anything they had already done, but on the contrary urged the Persian on even more; and Thorax of Larissa, who had joined in escorting Xerxes during his flight, now openly gave Mardonius passage for the invasion of Greece.
